more.summary: AI engineers often recognize ethical risks associated with the systems they build, but many lack the authority, incentives and organizational support needed to act on them, according to new research from the University of Manchester.

more.title: How adoption of a new crop reshaped land use in Bronze Age Europe
more.summary: A new study published in Science Advances reveals how Bronze Age communities in Central Europe adapted to changing environmental and social conditions by adopting broomcorn millet, a fast-growing, climate-resilient crop.

more.title: Chandra uncovers 'hypersoft X-ray sources' that may solve two astrophysical puzzles
more.summary: Using NASA's Chandra X-ray Observatory, scientists have discovered a new class of objects behaving unlike any they have seen before. Astronomers suggest these newly spotted objects in other galaxies may help solve not one, but two long-standing questions in astrophysics.

more.title: Uber invests $10M in Indian fleet operator Carrum at $168M valuation
more.author: Jagmeet Singh
more.summary: Carrum Mobility operates about 5,100 vehicles in India and is Uber's largest fleet partner for its premium Uber Black service in the country.

more.title: Terbium's elusive plus-4 form emerges under ordinary lab conditions, opening possibilities for rare-earth metals
more.summary: Chemists in a new study led by the University of Iowa report they have isolated and described in detail an atypical state of the rare-earth metal terbium, an advance that could expand its use in quantum technologies, including computing and advanced sensors. The study, "Structural and spectroscopic characterization of a Tb(IV) polyoxometalate," is published in the journal Nature Communications.

more.title: Tiny salt crevices could act as miniature 'Greenhouses' for Martian microbes
more.summary: We've been searching for life on Mars for a long time, but so far we've come up empty. The fundamental problem is a Catch-22 involving two of the key ingredients for life. Life as we know it needs liquid water and reasonable temperatures, both of which are available on Mars, but hardly ever at the same time.

more.title: When it comes to Beatles references, scientists can't let it be

The satellite now is flying 30 seconds behind its predecessor, Sentinel-6 Michael Freilich. more.title: Timing 1080 drops to prevent predators bouncing back
more.summary: While aerial 1080 drops sharply reduce numbers of rats and stoats, the predators—especially ship rats—can rebound to higher numbers within a few years. Studying 24 years of small-mammal tracking records across New Zealand's public conservation land, researchers found that the timing of these rebounds varies between regions.

more.title: Can AI tame torrential rain by 2050? The next frontier of weather control and forecasting
more.summary: Japan has been experiencing increasingly severe damage from torrential rainfall triggered by typhoons and stationary linear rain bands. In response, an ambitious and unconventional idea is taking shape: artificially inducing heavy rainfall over the ocean to reduce extreme downpours on land.

In an emeritus role, individuals with a high degree of technical and professional knowledge can continue to support the agency by donating their […]

more.title: Luck or merit? Not all inequality is equally acceptable
more.summary: Do you think it's fair that some people are better off financially than others? Does it perhaps matter whether those earnings stem from a lottery win or hard work? These are the kinds of questions economist Ingvild Almås of the University of Zurich is exploring.

more.title: The trapdoor spiders giving a leg up to science
more.summary: WA's trapdoor spiders are endangered. Jackson Rendall is here to help—because he thinks they're "just really cool."

more.title: Ozempic and Wegovy linked to nearly 40% fewer asthma attacks
more.summary: Semaglutide, the drug found in Ozempic and Wegovy, was linked to nearly 40% fewer asthma attacks in a large real-world study. It was also associated with about 20% fewer COPD flare-ups. Researchers say GLP-1 drugs may offer respiratory benefits in addition to their effects on diabetes and obesity, but clinical trials are needed to confirm the findings.

more.title: Eight PFAS compounds detected at low concentrations in Melbourne rain
more.summary: Researchers from RMIT University and EPA Victoria detected eight PFAS compounds in rainwater samples collected in Melbourne between 2024 and 2025.

more.title: Unconventional quantum materials could dramatically boost the search for dark matter
more.summary: For decades, physicists have searched for dark matter, the invisible substance thought to make up roughly 85% of all matter in the universe. Although its gravitational influence shapes galaxies and the large-scale structure of the cosmos, dark matter has never been directly detected.

more.title: Interstellar comet 3I/ATLAS is bursting with methanol
more.summary: Interstellar comet 3I/ATLAS contains exceptionally high levels of methanol, suggesting it formed under conditions very different from those that shaped most comets in our solar system. ALMA also revealed that tiny icy grains around the comet are releasing methanol like miniature comets, giving astronomers an unusually detailed look at an object from another star system.
